title: A Language for the Wardrobe
premise: Yara Brightwater, a night librarian in the sleepless city of Vell, is hired by Ilse Marrow, the last fluent speaker of Ashen—a language once spoken by the city's erased river-dwellers—to transcribe it before Ilse dies. As Yara learns the language, she discovers her own grandmother appears in Ilse's old photographs as an informer who betrayed the Ashen speakers to the authorities decades ago. Torn between protecting her family's memory and honoring the dying language, Yara must choose whether to tell Ilse the truth. In the end she confesses; Ilse, expecting it all along, forgives her by naming Yara the language's final speaker, and Yara, no longer a tenant of her own life, opens the library's doors at dawn to teach the first new student.
about_author: Y. M. Underhill is the pen name of a former night-shift archivist who spent eleven years cataloguing endangered-language recordings in municipal collections. Their fiction explores what institutions keep, and what they quietly discard.

chapters.title: The Hours That Belong to No One
chapters.summary: Yara works the night desk at the Vell Municipal Library, shelving books for insomniacs and watching the city's lights burn later each year. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as contentment; she insists she prefers being unseen.

chapters.title: A Request Slipped Between Pages
chapters.summary: An elderly woman leaves a note at the desk asking for 'a student, not a scribe.' Yara tracks her to a boarding house by the old canal. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: reluctant curiosity piercing routine.

chapters.title: Ilse Marrow Speaks Backward
chapters.summary: Yara meets Ilse, who tests her by reciting Ashen—words that sound like water over stones. Ilse explains the language has no living speaker but herself. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: awe tangled with suspicion of being needed.

chapters.title: Terms of Inheritance
chapters.summary: Ilse offers payment Yara can't refuse but demands nightly lessons and absolute honesty. Yara signs without reading the fine print of her own heart. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: transactional safety beginning to crack.

chapters.title: First Words: Water, Door, Stay
chapters.summary: First lesson: Ashen has twelve words for belonging and none for 'owner.' Yara struggles; Ilse is a harsh, funny teacher. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: frustration giving way to unexpected delight.

chapters.title: The Photographs in the Tin
chapters.summary: Yara finds a biscuit tin of photographs in Ilse's room—river people, demolished tenements—and freezes: her young grandmother stands among them. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past reaching into the present.

chapters.title: What the River Kept
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter through Ilse's telling: the Ashen-speaking river community, its eviction, and the informer whose testimony sealed it. POV: alternating Yara/Ilse. Emotional beat: dread building as details match Yara's family stories.

chapters.title: A Tenant's Inventory
chapters.summary: Yara audits her life—sublet room, borrowed habits, no one who'd notice absence—and realizes invisibility was survival learned from her grandmother. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: grief for a self never chosen.

chapters.title: Grammar of Refusal
chapters.summary: Lesson: Ashen verbs change depending on whether you witness or cause an event. Yara asks how to say 'I didn't do it'; Ilse says the language doesn't allow lying about that. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the language pressing on her secret like a bruise.

chapters.title: The Committee's Letters
chapters.summary: In the library archives, Yara finds the 1960s Relocation Committee files; her grandmother's signature appears on three denunciations. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: cold confirmation; shame inherited like debt.

chapters.title: Ilse's Good Arm
chapters.summary: Ilse's health falters; she dictates faster, teaching songs meant for children. Yara realizes she's memorizing a funeral. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: tenderness sharpened by urgency.

chapters.title: The Stranger in the Old Photographs
chapters.summary: Yara studies the tin photos nightly, trying to see her grandmother as stranger rather than blood. She drafts a confession letter and burns it. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: self-protective cowardice at war with duty.

chapters.title: A Second Student
chapters.summary: A young archivist, Dev, notices Yara's notebooks and asks to learn too. Yara refuses, jealous of the language now that it feels like hers. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: possessiveness revealing how much she's changed.

chapters.title: Ilse Remembers Wrong on Purpose
chapters.summary: Ilse tells a version of the betrayal that softens the informer; Yara realizes Ilse may be protecting someone—or testing her. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: paranoia and hope in equal measure.

chapters.title: Night Market Vocabulary
chapters.summary: Ilse takes Yara to the night market to use Ashen aloud among strangers; words land like coins. For one hour Yara belongs somewhere. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: intoxicating belonging, immediately feared as temporary.

chapters.title: The Landlord of Memory
chapters.summary: A developer's agent pressures Ilse to sell the boarding house—the last Ashen address. Yara witnesses power repeating its old theft. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: anger crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: Twelve Words for Belonging
chapters.summary: Ilse teaches the belonging-words; each requires naming who you belong to. Yara can only say the word for 'belonging to no one,' and Ilse flinches. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the cost of her guardedness made audible.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Yara visits her mother with pretext questions; finds grandmother's ledger recording payments from the Committee alongside rent for river families she secretly sheltered. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: moral whiplash—betrayer and protector in one hand.

chapters.title: Half a Truth
chapters.summary: Yara tells Ilse her family came from the river district but hides the ledger. The lie sits between them during every lesson after. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: guilt metastasizing; lessons lose warmth.

chapters.title: Dev Returns
chapters.summary: Dev has taught himself Ashen phonetics from archive tapes and corrects Yara's pronunciation. Humiliated, then grateful, she lets him in. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: pride yielding to companionship.

chapters.title: Ilse Stops Speaking Mid-Sentence
chapters.summary: A stroke takes half of Ilse's speech; her Ashen survives but her city-tongue frays. Now Ashen is the only way to reach her. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: terror inverted into intimacy—the language becomes a bridge.

chapters.title: Lessons in a Hospital Corridor
chapters.summary: Yara teaches Dev while learning to nurse Ilse; the roles of student and keeper blur. Ilse, aphasic in Vellish, jokes fluently in Ashen. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: bittersweet comedy inside decline.

chapters.title: The Recording Sessions
chapters.summary: Racing Ilse's deterioration, they record vocabulary, songs, curses, lullabies. A university offers to 'acquire' the archive; Ilse refuses to be collected. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: defiance of institutional ownership—theme of power surfacing.

chapters.title: What Informers Are Owed
chapters.summary: Ilse, lucid at 3 a.m., says she always knew who the informer was and why she did it—and that she's waited fifty years to hear it said aloud. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: floor dropping out; the confession is demanded, not offered.

chapters.title: The Ledger Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Yara reads her grandmother's ledger to Ilse in Ashen, translating betrayal and shelter line by line. Ilse listens without interrupting. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: catharsis through the language itself; truth finally grammatical.

chapters.title: Forgiveness Is Not a Word Here
chapters.summary: Ashen has no single word for forgiveness—only constructions meaning 'I keep you anyway.' Ilse uses one. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: devastating grace; Yara undone and remade.

chapters.title: The Developer's Deadline
chapters.summary: The boarding house sale closes in two weeks; Ilse will be moved to a facility that forbids overnight visitors. Time runs out on every front. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: pressure compressing toward climax.

chapters.title: Petition of the Sleepless
chapters.summary: Yara organizes the library's insomniac regulars—night nurses, bakers, cab drivers—to contest the eviction and host Ashen classes in the library after hours. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: the invisible claiming public space together.

chapters.title: Hearing at Dawn
chapters.summary: At the zoning hearing, Yara speaks Ashen publicly for the first time; the sound of the erased language in an official room stuns the council. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: courage; private inheritance becomes public act.

chapters.title: Ilse Escapes
chapters.summary: Ilse checks herself out of care against advice to attend the hearing, collapses afterward, and makes Yara promise the language won't die politely in an archive. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: fear and fierce love.

chapters.title: The Last Fluent Speaker Dreams
chapters.summary: Ilse drifts between Ashen and childhood, calling names of the drowned district. Yara answers each name correctly; Ilse smiles. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: vigil; death approaching as conversation.

chapters.title: Succession
chapters.summary: Lucid again briefly, Ilse formally names Yara—not an archive, not the university—as Ashen's carrier, before witnesses Dev and the night regulars. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: weight of inheritance accepted willingly at last.

chapters.title: The Night the City Slept
chapters.summary: For the first time in years, Vell goes dark during a grid failure; by candlelight, the library hosts an Ashen evening of songs. Ilse attends in a wheelchair. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: communal grace; belonging enacted.

chapters.title: Ilse Marrow, 1931–
chapters.summary: Ilse dies at dawn with Yara holding her hand, speaking the belonging-word for 'kept' as her last. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: grief without regret; a good ending earned.

chapters.title: Estate of Small Things
chapters.summary: Sorting Ilse's room, Yara finds a second photograph: her grandmother and Ilse as girls, arms linked—friends before the betrayal. The tin was left for her deliberately. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: sorrow deepened by tenderness; forgiveness prefigured.

chapters.title: The University Comes Calling
chapters.summary: The university threatens legal claim on the recordings; Yara, backed by Dev and the night community, refuses, publishing free instead. Power meets refusal. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: hard-won assertiveness; theme resolved in action.

chapters.title: First Class
chapters.summary: Seven students attend the first open Ashen class at the library, including a girl from the redeveloped river district. Yara teaches Ilse's first lesson verbatim. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: continuity; grief converted into transmission.

chapters.title: Owning Nothing, Keeping Everything
chapters.summary: Yara signs a lease—her first real home—above the canal, and hangs the tin photographs where visitors can see them, captions honest. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: integration; she stops being a tenant of her own life.

chapters.title: The Word for Stay
chapters.summary: One year later: the class has grown; Dev co-teaches; the city sleeps a little more. Yara writes Ilse's story into the library's permanent record under both their names. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: peace; memory given institutional permanence.

chapters.title: A Language for the Wardrobe
chapters.summary: Final scene: Yara teaches a child the phrase meaning 'a place where your true clothes are kept'—the book's title phrase, Ilse's definition of language itself. She says it back to the empty air, and something answers. POV: Yara. Emotional beat: quiet transcendence; the language lives because someone stayed.
